input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps! What do I need to do next?

I’m not sure about all of that, but I do see a little airplane icon at the top of my phone screen. Does that mean something? I haven’t noticed any error messages, it just won’t send the picture. I’m not sure if I’m on Wi-Fi or mobile data right now. 

Is the airplane thing important?

Okay, I turned off the airplane mode like you said. Now there’s no airplane icon, but I see something that says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” at the top. I tried sending the picture again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do now?

I’m a bit confused—my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I also tried turning on mobile data, but it still says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” at the top. What does that mean? Is there something wrong with my SIM card?

Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now I see some little bars at the top, and it says “2G” and “Data Enabled.” Does that mean it’s working now? Should I try sending the picture again?

I changed the network mode like you suggested, and now it says “5G” at the top with full bars and “Data Enabled.” Should I try sending the picture message again now, or is there something else I need to do first?
I just tried sending the picture again, but it still won’t go through. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? Is there something else I need to check?
I checked, and it looks like there isn’t any MMSC URL set in my phone’s settings. I’m not really sure what that means, but does that explain why I can’t send picture messages? What should I do next?

I’m not sure how to find the make and model of my phone, and I get a bit nervous about changing settings or restarting things. If I reset the APN settings and reboot, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you please reassure me about that before I try anything?

Alright, I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you said. It says the settings will reset when I reboot the phone. Should I go ahead and restart it now? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working, and I’m getting a bit worried now. Is there anything else we can try?

I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on, but my Wi-Fi itself is off. I’m not sure how to turn off Wi-Fi Calling, though. Also, I don’t see any error messages when I try to send the picture—it just doesn’t go through. Could you walk me through how to turn off Wi-Fi Calling?

I managed to turn off Wi-Fi Calling following your steps, but I still can’t send picture messages—it just won’t work. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all this.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message—what I think you call an MMS?—to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. This has been happening for a few hours now. Can you help me fix it?

Thank you for reaching out about your MMS issue. I can help you troubleshoot this problem. First, I’ll need to identify your account to check for any service or data issues that might be affecting your ability to send picture messages.

Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (in YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can begin assisting you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps! What do I need to do next?

Thank you, John. I have identified your account. To help you send picture messages (MMS), I’ll need to check a few things on your phone and account, such as your service status, mobile data, and some settings.

Could you please let me know:
- Are you able to make regular calls and send text messages?
- Are you currently connected to Wi-Fi or using mobile data?
- Do you see any error messages when trying to send the MMS?

Once you provide this information, I’ll guide you step-by-step to resolve the issue.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%

I’m not sure about all of that, but I do see a little airplane icon at the top of my phone screen. Does that mean something? I haven’t noticed any error messages, it just won’t send the picture. I’m not sure if I’m on Wi-Fi or mobile data right now. 

Is the airplane thing important?

Yes, the airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is turned on. When Airplane Mode is enabled, all wireless connections—including cellular service and mobile data—are turned off. This will prevent you from sending MMS (picture messages), making calls, or using mobile data.

To fix this, please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon so it is no longer highlighted.

Once you have turned off Airplane Mode, please try sending your picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have trouble, and I’ll help you with the next steps!

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned off the airplane mode like you said. Now there’s no airplane icon, but I see something that says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” at the top. I tried sending the picture again, but it still won’t go through. What should I do now?

Thank you for the update. Since you now see “No Signal” and “Data Disabled,” your phone currently does not have cellular service or mobile data enabled. Both are required to send MMS.

Let’s try the following steps:

1. Make sure your SIM card is properly inserted and active.
2. Enable mobile data on your phone.

Could you please check if your SIM card is working? If you know how, look for a SIM card icon or a message about the SIM on your phone. If you’re not sure, let me know, and I’ll guide you through checking your SIM status and enabling mobile data.
No SIM card detected in the phone.

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

I’m a bit confused—my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I also tried turning on mobile data, but it still says “No Signal” and “Data Disabled” at the top. What does that mean? Is there something wrong with my SIM card?

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, that means your phone cannot connect to the cellular network, which is why you have “No Signal” and “Data Disabled.” This is likely the main reason you can’t send picture messages.

Let’s try a simple step first: please remove your SIM card from your phone and then reinsert it. This is called “reseating” the SIM card and can often fix detection issues.

Once you’ve done that, check if your phone now recognizes the SIM card and if you see any signal bars or if mobile data is enabled. Let me know what you see after reseating the SIM card. If the issue continues, I’ll guide you through the next steps.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I took out the SIM card and put it back in like you said. Now I see some little bars at the top, and it says “2G” and “Data Enabled.” Does that mean it’s working now? Should I try sending the picture again?

Great job reseating the SIM card! Seeing signal bars and “Data Enabled” means your phone is now connected to the network. However, since it says “2G,” your phone is on an older, slower network type. MMS (picture messages) may not work reliably on 2G.

Let’s improve your connection before you try sending the picture again:
- Please change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G, if your phone supports it. This will give you faster data and better MMS support.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to change your network mode to 4G/5G?

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I changed the network mode like you suggested, and now it says “5G” at the top with full bars and “Data Enabled.” Should I try sending the picture message again now, or is there something else I need to do first?

That’s excellent! Now that your phone shows “5G,” full bars, and “Data Enabled,” your device is connected to a fast network and mobile data is active. You should now try sending your picture message (MMS) again.

If the message still doesn’t go through, please let me know, and I’ll help you check a few more settings. Otherwise, let me know if it works!
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I just tried sending the picture again, but it still won’t go through. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? Is there something else I need to check?

I understand how frustrating this can be, and I’m here to help you get this resolved. Since your phone now has a strong 5G signal and data is enabled, the next most common reason for MMS issues is incorrect APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for sending picture messages.

Let’s check your APN settings:
- On your phone, look for the APN or cellular network settings (usually found in Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network > Access Point Names).
- Check if there is an MMSC (Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL set. If you’re not sure how to find this, let me know.

If you’re able to check and see that the MMSC URL is missing or looks incorrect, you should reset your APN settings to default. After resetting, please restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device?

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
I checked, and it looks like there isn’t any MMSC URL set in my phone’s settings. I’m not really sure what that means, but does that explain why I can’t send picture messages? What should I do next?

Yes, the missing MMSC URL is likely the reason you can’t send picture messages. The MMSC URL is required for your phone to send and receive MMS (picture messages).

Here’s what you should do next:
1. Reset your APN settings to the default values. This will restore the correct MMSC URL and other necessary settings.
2. After resetting the APN, restart (reboot) your phone to apply the changes.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device? If so, please let me know your phone’s make and model (e.g., Samsung Galaxy S21, iPhone 13), and I’ll guide you through the process.

I’m not sure how to find the make and model of my phone, and I get a bit nervous about changing settings or restarting things. If I reset the APN settings and reboot, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Could you please reassure me about that before I try anything?

Rest assured, resetting your APN settings and rebooting your phone will NOT delete any of your photos, messages, contacts, or other personal data. 

Resetting APN settings only restores your phone’s network connection settings (like how it connects to the internet and sends MMS) to their default values. Rebooting simply restarts your phone, just like turning it off and on again.

Your personal content—photos, messages, apps, and files—will remain safe and unchanged.

If you’re ready, I can guide you step-by-step through resetting your APN settings and rebooting your phone. Would you like to proceed?

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you said. It says the settings will reset when I reboot the phone. Should I go ahead and restart it now? I just want to make sure I’m doing the right thing.

Yes, you are doing exactly the right thing! Please go ahead and restart (reboot) your phone now. This will apply the new APN settings and should resolve the issue with sending picture messages.

After your phone restarts, try sending the picture message again. Let me know if it works or if you still have any trouble—I’m here to help until it’s fixed!

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working, and I’m getting a bit worried now. Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for letting me know. Since you’ve reset your APN settings, rebooted your phone, and still can’t send picture messages, let’s check a few more things that could affect MMS:

1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your phone? Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling turned on can interfere with MMS. If you know how, please check if Wi-Fi Calling is on and try turning it off.
2. Are you able to browse the internet or use other apps that require mobile data (with Wi-Fi turned off)? This helps confirm that mobile data is working for other services.
3. Do you see any error messages when trying to send the picture message now?

If you’re unsure how to check Wi-Fi Calling or mobile data, let me know, and I’ll guide you through it step by step. Your answers will help me determine the next best step to resolve this for you.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
Wi-Fi is turned OFF.

I checked, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned on, but my Wi-Fi itself is off. I’m not sure how to turn off Wi-Fi Calling, though. Also, I don’t see any error messages when I try to send the picture—it just doesn’t go through. Could you walk me through how to turn off Wi-Fi Calling?

Absolutely, I can guide you through turning off Wi-Fi Calling. The steps may vary slightly depending on your phone type, but here are the general instructions for most devices:

For Android phones:
1. Open the Phone app (where you make calls).
2. Tap the three dots (menu) in the top right corner and select “Settings.”
3. Look for “Wi-Fi Calling” in the list.
4. Tap on “Wi-Fi Calling” and toggle it OFF.

For iPhones:
1. Open the Settings app.
2. Scroll down and tap “Phone.”
3. Tap “Wi-Fi Calling.”
4. Toggle “Wi-Fi Calling on This iPhone” OFF.

After you turn off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending your picture message again. Let me know if you need more detailed steps or if you’re using a different type of phone. If the MMS still doesn’t go through, please let me know, and we’ll continue troubleshooting together.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I managed to turn off Wi-Fi Calling following your steps, but I still can’t send picture messages—it just won’t work. Is there anything else we can try? I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed by all this.

Thank you for your patience and for following all the steps so far. Since you’ve tried all the main troubleshooting steps—resetting APN settings, rebooting, ensuring mobile data is enabled, and turning off Wi-Fi Calling—but you still can’t send picture messages, this may require more advanced support.

At this point, I will transfer you to a human agent who can provide further assistance and investigate any deeper technical issues with your account or service.
